purpose: The OPERATIONAL view: what a driver may rely on, right now, on this host. Kept separate from primitives/harness-matrix.json, which is aesop's historical PRODUCT-support matrix pinned at a stated commit and is not rewritten here. Each capability carries three independent answers -- does the product support it, has polytropos implemented it, has anyone verified it by running it -- because collapsing them into one boolean is how a driver comes to believe it holds a control it does not.
unknown_is_valid: A capability nobody has run reports verified=unknown, and a caller needing certainty must treat that as no. Filling these in optimistically would make the file worse than not having it.

dispatch.note: one authorized live invocation, scoped to validating flag handling; tests never invoke the real CLI

tool_pin.note: the `--allowedTools=<space-joined>` form is REQUIRED: the variadic form swallows the following positional, which silently consumed the prompt on every review dispatch. This row is why the registry has a verified column

confined_verify.note: polytropos capability, not a product one: verify commands run under an OS boundary. macOS only -- enforced mode refuses on Linux and Windows rather than downgrading

confined_dispatch.note: sandbox-exec blocks Keychain access and subscription credentials live there, so a confined dispatch reports 'Not logged in'. Keychain access is gated by entitlements, not profile rules; granting mach-lookup and keychain writes does not change it

status.note: no run-status query is implemented here, and whether the CLI exposes one has not been checked

cancel.note: the process tree can be terminated; that says nothing about whether the model call it made was already billed

dispatch.note: never invoked live from this repository -- tests stub every dispatch

sandbox_read_only.note: review and acceptance are pinned read-only and extra arguments cannot override it. The flag's runtime effect has not been verified here

structured_events.note: thread.started / item.completed / turn.completed are parsed; model attestation falls back to unknown when no correlated record appears

async_tools.note: tool calls the model does not block on, returned later under the original call id. Reported for the vendor's API and not checked here against vendor documentation; whether `codex exec` exposes it has not been checked either, and nothing in this repo uses it. Recorded so a scheduler cannot assume it

mid_turn_steering.note: new user instructions injected into a running turn with finished work kept. Reported for a persistent API connection; the driver runs `codex exec` to completion and has no channel to steer through, so this is unsupported here whatever the product does

effort_per_turn.note: changing reasoning effort between turns of one session with the cached prefix intact. Distinct from per-dispatch effort, which the driver sets once on the command line before the run starts and never changes afterwards

cancel.note: process-tree termination only; see the claude-code row

dispatch.note: never invoked live from this repository, by invariant: a real call spends the user's AI Credits

tool_pin.note: no per-tool flag was found that could be cited, and inventing one would have produced a control that reads as enforced and is not. Restricted review therefore means only the absence of the blanket `--allow-all-tools` grant (the default since step 06; `--review-permissions bypass` restores it and says so) -- there is no narrower pin to fall back to, and SECURITY.md states that rather than papering over it

cancel.note: process-tree termination only; see the claude-code row

dispatch.note: conformance target: returns a canned result and spawns nothing
step 23 delivers this adapter. The row exists so the registry says 'not built yet' rather than being silent, which reads the same as 'not applicable'
